View state (load/filter the audit trail) assembling core + data for the view.

uncertain: Recording placement: the data/ mutations only receive an id, so the true 'before' snapshot lives in the ui composables (useInvoiceDetail.ts holds the invoice, useReschedule.ts holds the old start/end). Capturing a real before/after diff may mean calling recordChange from those composables (or widening the mutation signatures) rather than inside data/mutations.ts — this is my least-certain call.

Slice vs shared: I made audit its own slice because compliance is a distinct reason-to-change spanning both domains, but an audit trail that reaches into two domains slightly strains the 'near-total silo' model; a case exists for each slice owning its own trail instead.
Whether core/rules.ts is warranted or core is just types.ts — depends on how much real change-diff/formatting logic exists.

Whether the client should emit records at all: in a real backend the server owns the audit trail and the frontend only reads it, which would drop the mutations edits + audit/data/mutations.ts and leave only queries + the view.
questions: 'Who did it' has no source: there is no auth/user/actor/session concept anywhere in the codebase. Where does the current user's identity come from, and should an identity/session slice (or app-level provider) be introduced before this?
Is the audit trail authored server-side (real backend) or must the client emit each record? MSW is the only 'API' here, which changes whether the mutations/mocks edits are needed.

Scope of 'what changed': today only invoice-void and appointment-reschedule mutations exist. Should audit cover just these, or every future mutation (needs a general recording pattern), and does compliance need full field-level before/after diffs or just an action label + timestamp?
Should the compliance view be access-controlled / route-guarded, and where would that guard live given there's no auth?

Adding a slice edits CODEOWNERS-protected files (architecture.config.ts, and effectively router/msw composition) — is architecture review expected as part of this feature, or should the trail be shoehorned into existing slices to avoid that?
